To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the vacuum $e^{+}$ - $e^{-}$ -plasma is created by a strong laser field with a power of the order of 10 PW in the range of x-ray lasers.
the WKB - type approximatins in the theory of particle creation in strong field are unreliable and that the strict kinetic approach is the only one which is able to give reliable predictions.

(i) the kinetic approach is a reliable tool for the description of vacuum creation of $e^{+}$ - $e^{-}$ plasma in strong nonstationay fields; (ii) WKB-type approximtions in the theory of particle creation in QED have an insufficient foundation; (iii) the theory predicts the creation of a $e^{+}-e^{-}$ plasma at optical and x-ray lasers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a reliable theory for vacuum creation of an electron-positron plasma in strong nonstationar fields.
the question: How reliable are WKB-type approximative methods in the QED theory of vacuum creation?
the question of the reliability of predictions based on the kinetic approach to QED in strong fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the theory of vacuum $e^{+}$ $e^{-}$ - pair creation in strong fields is not yet ready for predictions of the parameters of the future experiments.
the observation of vacuum particle creation is still an open question.
the kinetic approach is the only reliable one in the theory of particle creation in strong laser fields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the theory of vacuum $e^{+}$ - $e^{-}$ - pair creation is not yet sufficiently well developed for reliable predictions of the parameters of the $e^{+}-e^{-}$ - plasmas created in strong laser fields.
the creation of an $ e^{+}e^{−}$ - plasma in strong laser fields is a real phenomenon but its observation in the range of presently available laser facilities is not yet possible.

The main takeaway from our work is that
WKB-type approximation in the theory of particle creation in nonstationary fields is insufficiently justified and should be used with great caution.
in order to get reliable predictions on the basis on the kinetic approach one should avoid unphysical field models.
the kinetic theory is the only approach which allows to predict reliably vacuum creation of an electron-positron plasma in the strong fields of optical and xray lasers.
